'''Boris Babacar Diaw-Riffiod''' (born 16 April 1982), better known as '''Boris Diaw''', is a French [[basketball]] executive and former player who is the president of [[Metropolitans 92]] of [[LNB Pro A]]. Diaw began his playing career in Pro A and returned to that league after 14 seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He primarily played the [[Power forward (basketball)|power forward]] position. In 2006, Diaw was named the NBA's [[NBA Most Improved Player Award|Most Improved Player]] as a member of the [[Phoenix Suns]]. He won an [[NBA championship]] with the [[San Antonio Spurs]] in 2014.

Diaw was a member and captain of the senior [[France national basketball team|French national team]]. He won a [[FIBA Basketball World Cup|FIBA World Cup]] bronze medal in [[2014 FIBA World Championship|2014]], a [[EuroBasket]] title in [[EuroBasket 2013|2013]], a silver medal in [[EuroBasket 2011]], and two bronze in [[EuroBasket 2005]] and [[EuroBasket 2015]]. He earned an [[All-EuroBasket Team]] selection in 2005.

Diaw has served as president of Metropolitans 92 from July 2019 to April 2020.

==Professional basketball career==
===Pau-Orthez (2001–2003)===
From 2001 to 2003, Diaw played for [[Élan Béarnais Pau-Orthez|Pau-Orthez]] of the [[LNB Pro A]], a French professional basketball league. In 2002, he competed in the league's All-Star game and the Slam Dunk contest.

===Atlanta Hawks (2003–2005)===
Diaw was selected by the [[Atlanta Hawks]] with the 21st overall pick in the [[2003 NBA draft]]. On July 10, 2003, he signed a multi-year deal with the Hawks.

===Phoenix Suns (2005–2008)===
In August 2005, he was traded with two future first-round picks to the Phoenix Suns in exchange for future teammate [[Joe Johnson (basketball)|Joe Johnson]].<ref name=suns>{{cite web |title=Johnson Trade to Atlanta Completed |work=NBA.com |url=http://www.nba.com/suns/news/johnson_traded_050819.html |date=August 19, 2005 |access-date=June 16, 2014}}</ref>

In Phoenix, Diaw blossomed into an all-round player, playing any position from center to point guard and garnered the nickname "3D" because of his multidimensional play (his motto being "drive, dish, defend") and the combination of his number (3) and surname. Diaw averaged 13.3 points, 6.9 rebounds, 6.2 assists and 1.0 blocks per game on 52.6% field goal shooting and 73.1% from the free throw line in the [[2005–06 NBA season|2005–06 season]] where he played both [[Forward (basketball)|forward]] positions and then [[Center (basketball)|center]] after injuries to [[Amar'e Stoudemire]] and [[Kurt Thomas (basketball)|Kurt Thomas]].

During the [[2006 NBA playoffs]], as the Suns' starting center, Diaw averaged 18.7 points, 6.7 rebounds, 5.2 assists and 1.1 blocks per game. In Game 1 of the 2006 Western Conference Finals against the Dallas Mavericks, Diaw scored a career-high 34 points, including the game-winner with 0.5 seconds remaining in regulation, to help the Suns to a 121–118 victory, although Phoenix would go on the lose the series in six games.

===Charlotte Bobcats (2008–2012)===
[[File:Boris diaw bobcats.jpg|thumb|175px|right|Diaw with the Bobcats in 2009]]

On December 10, 2008, Diaw, along with [[Raja Bell]] and [[Sean Singletary]], was traded to the [[Charlotte Hornets|Charlotte Bobcats]] in exchange for [[Jason Richardson]] and [[Jared Dudley]].<ref name=bobcats>{{cite web |title=Suns trade Bell, Diaw for Bobcats' Richardson |work=NBA.com |url=http://www.nba.com/2008/news/12/10/sunsbobcats.trade.ap/index.html |date=December 18, 2008 |access-date=June 16, 2014}}</ref>

On September 28, 2011, Diaw signed with [[JSA Bordeaux]] of [[LNB Pro B|France]] for the duration the [[2011 NBA lockout]].<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/france/88519/boris-diaw-officially-signs-for-jsa-bordeaux.html Boris Diaw officially signs for JSA Bordeaux]</ref> In December 2011, he returned to the Charlotte Bobcats.

On March 21, 2012, Diaw was waived by the Bobcats.<ref>{{cite web |date=March 21, 2012 |title=Bobcats waive Boris Diaw |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/7717314/charlotte-bobcats-waive-boris-diaw-agreeing-contract-buyout |access-date=June 16, 2014 |work=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press}}</ref>

===San Antonio Spurs (2012–2016)===
Two days later, he signed with the [[San Antonio Spurs]] for the rest of the season.<ref name=spurs>[https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/7729120/san-antonio-spurs-get-boris-diaw-day-release-charlotte-bobcats Boris Diaw signed by Spurs]</ref>

On July 12, 2012, Diaw re-signed with the Spurs<ref>[http://www.nba.com/spurs/news/120712_diaw Spurs Re-Sign Boris Diaw]</ref> to a reported two-year, $9.2 million deal. Diaw helped the Spurs reach the [[2013 NBA Finals]] where they faced the Miami Heat. San Antonio lost the series in seven games.

[[File:Boris Diaw Spurs.jpg|thumb|195px|left|Diaw playing for the Spurs in 2014]]

On June 15, 2014, Diaw won his first NBA championship after the Spurs defeated the Miami Heat 4–1 in the [[2014 NBA Finals]]. He was inserted into the starting lineup beginning with Game 3, in order to counter Miami's "small ball lineup". Known for his high basketball IQ, Diaw also increased offensive efficiency for the Spurs via his vision and passing game, while being more versatile on defense than Tiago Splitter<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/playoffs/2014/story/_/id/11084748/boris-diaw-dishes-san-antonio-spurs |access-date=2026-06-25 |website=www.espn.com}}</ref><sup>,</sup><ref>{{Cite web |last=Buckley |first=Zach |title=Is Boris Diaw Biggest Reason San Antonio Spurs Are Smelling 2014 NBA Title? |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2096287-is-boris-diaw-biggest-reason-san-antonio-spurs-are-smelling-2014-nba-title |access-date=2026-06-25 |website=bleacherreport.com |language=en}}</ref>. As a result, Diaw led all players in the series in total assists (29) and was second in total rebounds (43) behind teammate [[Tim Duncan]] (50). Diaw averaged 35 minutes per game in the Finals, an increase of over 10 minutes from the regular season.<ref>{{cite news |last=Abrams |first=Jonathan |title=Mon Frère Boris |date=June 16, 2014 |work=Grantland.com |url=http://grantland.com/features/boris-diaw-tony-parker-san-antonio-spurs-nba-playoffs-2014/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140624033637/http://grantland.com/features/boris-diaw-tony-parker-san-antonio-spurs-nba-playoffs-2014/ |archive-date=June 24, 2014 |url-status=live }}</ref>

On July 15, 2014, Diaw re-signed with the Spurs<ref>[http://www.nba.com/spurs/spurs-re-sign-boris-diaw SPURS RE-SIGN BORIS DIAW]</ref> to a reported three-year, $22 million contract.<ref>[http://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/234144/Boris-Diaw-Agrees-To-Three-Year-$22M-Deal-With-Spurs Boris Diaw Agrees To Three-Year, $22M Deal With Spurs]</ref>

On August 1, 2015, Diaw played for Team Africa at the [[NBA Africa Game 2015|2015 NBA Africa exhibition game]].<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/13359599/nba-current-former-stars-put-show-africa-exhibition NBA stars, legends shine as Team World rallies to beat Team Africa]</ref>

===Utah Jazz (2016–2017)===
On July 8, 2016, Diaw was traded, along with a 2022 second-round pick and cash considerations, to the [[Utah Jazz]] in exchange for the rights to [[Olivier Hanlan]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-acquire-boris-diaw-and-draft-pick-spurs|title=Jazz Acquire Boris Diaw and Draft Pick from Spurs|work=NBA.com|date=July 8, 2016|access-date=July 8, 2016}}</ref> In early November 2016, Diaw missed eight games with a right leg contusion.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899601|title=Marc Gasol scores 22 points, Grizzlies beat Jazz 102-96|work=ESPN.com|date=November 14, 2016|access-date=November 15, 2016}}</ref> On July 13, 2017, he was waived by the Jazz.<ref>{{cite news|title=Jazz Waive Boris Diaw|url=http://www.nba.com/jazz/jazz-waive-boris-diaw|access-date=July 13, 2017|work=NBA.com|date=July 13, 2017}}</ref>

===Levallois Metropolitans (2017–2018)===
On September 17, 2017, Diaw signed with the [[Levallois Metropolitans]], a French team, for the 2017–18 season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Boris Diaw officially signs with Levallois Metropolitans|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/france/pro-a/247147/boris-diaw-officially-signs-with-levallois-metropolitans.html|access-date=September 17, 2017|work=Sportando.com|date=September 17, 2017}}</ref> With Levallois, he played in the [[LNB Pro A]] and [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]]. He averaged 11.1 points, 6.4 rebounds in 31.2 minutes per game in 31 Pro A games.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Boris-Diaw/Summary/459|title=Boris Diaw Player Profile|work=Realgm.com|access-date=13 July 2019}}</ref>

===Retirement===
Diaw announced his retirement via his Twitter account on September 6, 2018.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Wells |first1=Adam |title=Boris Diaw Retires at Age 36; Played with Spurs, Suns, Hornets, Hawks, Jazz |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2794533-boris-diaw-retires-at-age-36-played-with-spurs-suns-hornets-hawks-jazz |website=BleacherReport.com |access-date=September 6, 2018}}</ref>

==National team career==
[[File:Boris Diaw 2015.jpg|thumb|Diaw playing for France in 2015.]]
In 2000, Diaw won the [[2000 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship|FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship]] with the French junior national team. In July 2006, Diaw was named the [[captain (sports)|captain]] of the senior men's [[French national basketball team]]. He won the bronze medal at the [[EuroBasket 2005]].

Diaw led the French team at the [[2006 FIBA World Championship]], with 107 points and 22 assists, in 9 games. In 2013, Diaw and the French team won the gold medal at the [[2013 EuroBasket|EuroBasket tournament]]. The following year, he led the national team without its star Tony Parker to the bronze medal in the [[2014 FIBA Basketball World Cup|2014 FIBA World Cup]].

==Player profile==
At {{height|ft=6|in=8}} and {{Convert|250|lb|kg|abbr=unit}}, Diaw was a natural forward. However, his passing skills and ability to score inside earned him a reputation for being capable of playing all positions well. Diaw began the 2005–06 season as a reserve, substituted at point guard when starting point guard [[Steve Nash]] was injured, started at [[small forward]], and was finally moved to center when all three Suns centers were injured. Diaw's breakout season (13.3 points, 6.9 rebounds and 6.2 assists per game) was recognized with the Most Improved Player Award. Diaw was lauded for his unselfish but assertive play.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Duffy|first=Thomas|title=Gregg Popovich Misses Jazz F Boris Diaw as a Wine Drinking Partner|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2703722-gregg-popovich-misses-jazz-f-boris-diaw-as-a-wine-drinking-partner|access-date=2021-11-22|website=Bleacher Report|language=en}}</ref><sup>,</sup><ref>{{Cite web|last=DewNO|date=2013-12-12|title=Diaw's cool is crazy; his crazy is cool|url=https://www.poundingtherock.com/2013/12/12/5200582/boris-diaw-pass-assist-shoot-crazy-cool|access-date=2021-11-22|website=Pounding The Rock|language=en}}</ref>

While somewhat overshadowed by the Spurs 'Big Three' of [[Tim Duncan|Duncan]], [[Tony Parker|Parker]] and [[Manu Ginobili|Ginobili]], Diaw played a crucial role in the team's success. His excellent passing and playmaking abilities made him a prototype of what came to be known as the [[point forward]] position, exhibited by players such as [[Luka Dončić]] and to a lesser degree by [[LeBron James]] and [[Nikola Jokić]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/nba/news/boris-diaw-suns-terry-porter-shoot-story/6r1nelxd7vkj1rfaofkhokmce|title = Boris Diaw tells incredible story about arguing with Suns coach Terry Porter, then refusing to shoot | Sporting News| date=12 August 2021 }}</ref> Diaw was also an efficient post scorer and athletic scorer, capable of going coast-to-coast before either finding a teammate or finishing at the rim. In addition, his ability to play multiple positions made him a precursor to the current era of ''small ball teams'' and [[tweener (basketball)|positionless basketball]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sbnation.com/2017/9/14/16308110/boris-diaw-retirement-best-moments-suns-spurs-cappuccino-france|title = 13 reasons NBA fans should never stop loving Boris Diaw|date = 14 September 2017}}</ref>

==Executive career==
In 2009, Diaw became vice-president and shareholder of the [[JSA Bordeaux Basket|JSA Bordeaux]] basketball club in his native France and took over as president one year later. In 2017, he stepped down as president of the club.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.bebasket.fr/championnat-nm2/boris-diaw-annonce-son-retrait-des-jsa-bordeaux.html|title=Boris Diaw annonce son retrait des JSA Bordeaux|website=BeBasket|date=15 March 2017|language=fr|access-date=2017-03-17}}</ref>

In 2010, he founded UKIND, an eco-responsible clothing brand.

On July 4, 2019, Diaw was announced as the new president of [[Metropolitans 92]], succeeding Jean-Pierre Aubry.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Basket/Actualites/Jeep-elite-boris-diaw-officiellement-president-des-metropolitans-92/1036887|title=Jeep Élite : Boris Diaw officiellement président des Metropolitans 92 - Basket - Jeep Elite|work=L'Équipe|access-date=12 July 2019}}</ref> He resigned in April 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-04-27 |title=Boris Diaw quitte déjà la présidence des Métropolitans 92 |url=https://www.20minutes.fr/sport/2768567-20200427-boris-diaw-quitte-deja-presidence-metropolitans-92 |access-date=2024-11-28 |website=www.20minutes.fr |language=fr}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Diaw's {{height|ft=6|in=2}} mother, [[Élisabeth Riffiod]], is regarded as one of the best centers in French women's basketball history. She is a member of the [[French Basketball Hall of Fame]]. Diaw's father, Issa Diaw, is a former [[Senegal]]ese [[high jump]] champion. Diaw has a half-brother, Paco Diaw, who was a guard at [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball|Georgia Tech]],<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.ramblinwreck.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/diaw_paco00.html |title=Paco Diaw Bio |access-date=2014-06-16 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140725175649/http://www.ramblinwreck.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/diaw_paco00.html |archive-date=2014-07-25 |url-status=dead }}</ref> but transferred to [[Lee University]], a small [[National Association of Intercollegiate Athletics|NAIA]] school in the [[Southern States Athletic Conference]]. His other brother, Martin Diaw, played basketball for [[NCAA Division II|Division II]]'s [[California University of Pennsylvania]].<ref name="diaw_courtside">[http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/diaw_courtside_feature_031216.html Hawks Strike Gold with Diaw] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050311175929/http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/diaw_courtside_feature_031216.html |date=March 11, 2005 }}</ref>

Boris Diaw and Tony Parker are long-time friends who met at the French national training institute INSEP as teenagers, roomed together early in their careers, and later played together for the San Antonio Spurs. Diaw attended and served as a groomsman man at Parker's wedding to actress [[Eva Longoria]] in Paris in 2007.<ref name="firstgame">{{cite web |url=http://nba.aolsportsblog.com/2007/05/08/boris-diaw-are-you-ready-to-be-tony-parkers-best-man/ |title=Boris Diaw, Are You Ready to Be Tony Parker's Best Man? |work=aolsportsblog.com |date=May 8, 2007 |access-date=May 12, 2007 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130117082546/http://nba.aolsportsblog.com/2007/05/08/boris-diaw-are-you-ready-to-be-tony-parkers-best-man/ |archive-date=January 17, 2013 }}</ref> .

In 2005, Diaw established a non-profit foundation, Babac'Ards, to organize sports activities for Senegalese youth and aid "developmental education".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.iwg-gti.org/catalyst/february-2011/babac-ards-empowering-women-girl/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140722070858/http://www.iwg-gti.org/catalyst/february-2011/babac-ards-empowering-women-girl/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=July 22, 2014 |title=Babac'Ards - Empowering women & girls in Senegal through sport |work=iwg-gti.org |access-date=June 16, 2014 }}</ref>

Diaw is known to have a passion for photography, sailing, and wine tasting.<ref>{{cite news | title=Boris Diaw a worldwide photographer | work=ESPN | date=March 28, 2012 | url=https://www.espn.com/blog/playbook/visuals/post/_/id/56/boris-diaw-a-worldwide-photographer | last=Manahan | first=Theresa }}</ref><ref>{{cite news | title=Boris Diaw's new web series where he sails across the Atlantic is a delight | work=SB Nation | date=January 2, 2019 | url=https://www.sbnation.com/lookit/2019/1/2/18165330/boris-diaw-transatlantic-sailing-web-series-video | last=Dator | first=James }}</ref><ref>{{cite news | last=Wong | first=Alex | title=Boris Diaw, the Frenchiest Dude in the NBA, Is Down to Go to Mars | date=October 27, 2016 | url=https://www.gq.com/story/boris-diaw-interview | work=GQ }}</ref>
